checklist.item: Bring list of all current prescription and OTC medications with dosages
checklist.why: Prevents drug interactions and ensures medication history accuracy.

checklist.item: Write down a timeline of when your symptoms started and how they evolved
checklist.why: Helps the provider narrow down differential diagnosis.

checklist.item: Prepare 3-5 specific questions about your diagnosis and treatment options
checklist.why: Ensures key concerns are addressed during consultation.

checklist.item: Bring photo ID and health insurance card
Log symptom frequency, severity, or home readings (BP, glucose) since last visit
Note any medication side effects or difficulties taking prescribed drugs
checklist.why: Allows dosage adjustment or medication substitution.

checklist.item: Check if any prescription refills are needed before your appointment
checklist.why: Physician can send e-prescriptions during the visit.

checklist.item: Fast for 8-12 hours if routine bloodwork (CMP/Lipid panel) is scheduled
checklist.why: Ensures accurate glucose and lipid blood test results.

checklist.item: Update personal medical history, surgical history, and family history changes
checklist.why: Keeps preventative health screening schedule accurate.

checklist.item: List any preventative screenings or immunizations due (e.g. flu, tetanus, colonoscopy)
Request relevant medical records, lab reports, and imaging CDs from your PCP
checklist.why: Avoids duplicate testing and speeds up diagnostic evaluation.

checklist.item: Write a concise summary of why your PCP referred you to this specialist
checklist.why: Focuses the specialist consultation on the primary clinical question.

checklist.item: Confirm insurance authorization and referral paperwork prior to arrival
